Below we show the efficiency comparison across different configurations.\n\n \n \n \n\n \n \n \n\n \n \n \n\nIf you prefer Chinese documentation, please see the [Chinese README](./README_CN.md).\n## 📢 Latest Updates\n\n- **LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle (default):** SMPLX-FREE variant with an **MLPPixelShuffle** neural renderer (lighter dense head than DPT). Hub weights pending; use local checkpoint + &#96;--model_path&#96; until published.\n- **LHMPP-700M (updated release):** We released a new LHMPP-700M build that supports **standard 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY (&#96;3GS-PLY&#96;)** as an output format.\n\n### New features\n\n- **Export &#96;gs.ply&#96;:** Run [&#96;scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py&#96;](./scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py) to save **3D Gaussian Splatting** as a standard **&#96;.ply&#96;**—either **canonical T-pose** (leave &#96;--pose_dir&#96; empty) or **a single SMPL-X JSON frame** (&#96;--pose_dir&#96;). Full usage is in **Export Gaussian Splatting PLY (&#96;to_gs_ply.py&#96;)** under **Getting Started** below.\n- **GS render results:** In [&#96;app.py&#96;](./app.py), use **&#96;gs_render&#96;** for **RGB output from Gaussian splatting only** (no neural refinement). Launch with **&#96;--gs&#96;** when the model is **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** or **&#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;**, or switch **Output Renderer** to **gs_render** in the UI. See **Local Gradio Run** below.\n\n### TODO List\n\n- [x] Core Inference Pipeline🔥🔥🔥\n- [x] Release the codes and pretrained weights\n- [x] HuggingFace Demo Integration 🤗🤗🤗\n- [x] **Benchmarks — dynamic reconstruction:** evaluation code and validation data for **NeuMan**, **SelfCapture**, **Vid2Avatar** (see [Dynamic benchmark evaluation](#dynamic-benchmark-evaluation))\n- [ ] **Benchmarks — novel view/pose synthesis:** TODO (**THuman-2.1**, **DNA-Rendering**, etc.)\n- [ ] ModelScope Space Online Demo\n- [ ] Release Training data \u0026 Testing Data (License Available)\n- [ ] Training Codes Release \n\n## 🚀 Getting Started\n\n### Environment Setup\nClone the repository.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit clone https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM-plusplus\ncd LHM-plusplus\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# install torch 2.3.0 cuda 12.1\npip install torch==2.3.0 torchvision==0.18.0 torchaudio==2.3.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121\npip install -U xformers==0.0.26.post1 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121\n\n# install dependencies\npip install -r requirements.txt\npip install rembg[cpu]  # only use during extracting sparse view inputs.\n\n# install pointops\ncd ./lib/pointops/ \u0026\u0026 python setup.py install \u0026\u0026 cd ../../\n\npip install spconv-cu121\n# pip install torch_scatter, see [wheel](https://data.pyg.org/whl/) for your CUDA version\n# For example (PyTorch 2.3 + CUDA 12.1 + Python 3.10):\npip install torch_scatter-2.1.2+pt23cu121-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl\n\n# install pytorch3d\npip install --no-index --no-cache-dir pytorch3d -f https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/pytorch3d/packaging/wheels/py310_cu121_pyt230/download.html\n\n# install diff-gaussian-rasterization\npip install git+https://github.com/ashawkey/diff-gaussian-rasterization/\n# or\n# git clone --recursive https://github.com/ashawkey/diff-gaussian-rasterization\n# pip install ./diff-gaussian-rasterization\n\n# install simple-knn\npip install git+https://github.com/camenduru/simple-knn/\n\n# install gsplat\n# pip install gsplat from pre-compiled [wheel](https://docs.gsplat.studio/whl/gsplat/)\n# For example (PyTorch 2.3 + CUDA 12.1 + Python 3.10):\n# gsplat-1.4.0+pt23cu121-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl\npip install gsplat-1.4.0+pt23cu121-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe installation has been tested with python3.10, CUDA 12.1.\nOr you can install dependencies step by step, following [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md).\n\n### Model Weights \n\n#### One-Click Download (recommended)\n\nDownload assets (motion_video), prior models, and pretrained weights in one command:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# One-click: motion_video + prior models + pretrained weights\npython scripts/download_all.py\n\n# Skip parts (e.g. already have motion_video)\npython scripts/download_all.py --skip-asset --skip-models\n\n# Force re-download motion_video\npython scripts/download_all.py --force-asset\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Pretrained Model Download (individual)\n\nUse the download script to fetch prior models (human_model_files, voxel_grid, arcface, etc.) and LHM++ weights. Skips items that already exist. Tries HuggingFace first, falls back to ModelScope.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Download prior models + pretrained weights (default)\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py\n\n# Prior models only (human_model_files, voxel_grid, BiRefNet, etc.)\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py --prior\n\n# LHM++ model weights only (LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle default, LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE, LHMPP-700M, LHMPP-700MC, LHMPPS-700M)\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py --models\n\n# Custom save directory\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py --save-dir /path/to/pretrained_models\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Download from ModelScope (manual)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom modelscope import snapshot_download\n\n# LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle (default model weights; use --model_path until Hub is published)\nmodel_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# Or: LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE, LHMPP-700M, LHMPP-700MC, LHMPPS-700M\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700MC', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPPS-700M', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n\n# LHMPP-Prior (prior models: human_model_files, voxel_grid, BiRefNet, etc.)\nmodel_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Prior', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Motion Video Download\n\nRequired for Gradio motion examples. If &#96;./motion_video&#96; at project root is missing, downloads from [Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Assets](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Assets) (model, extracts motion_video.tar to project root):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Requires: pip install modelscope\npython scripts/download_motion_video.py\n\n# Custom parent directory (default: . = project root)\npython scripts/download_motion_video.py --save-dir .\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAfter downloading weights and data, the project structure:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n├── app.py\n├── assets\n│   ├── efficiency_analysis\n│   ├── example_aigc_images\n│   ├── example_multi_images\n│   ├── example_videos\n│   └── dynamic_metrics_table.md\n├── benchmark\n├── configs\n│   └── train\n│       ├── LHMPP-1view.yaml\n│       ├── LHMPP-any-view.yaml\n│       ├── LHMPP-any-view-convhead.yaml\n│       └── LHMPP-any-view-DPTS.yaml\n├── core\n│   ├── datasets\n│   ├── losses\n│   ├── models\n│   ├── modules\n│   ├── outputs\n│   ├── runners\n│   ├── structures\n│   ├── utils\n│   └── launch.py\n├── dnnlib\n├── engine\n│   ├── BiRefNet\n│   ├── pose_estimation\n│   └── ouputs.py\n├── exps\n│   ├── checkpoints\n│   ├── releases\n│   └── ...\n├── lib\n│   └── pointops\n├── pretrained_models\n│   ├── dense_sample_points\n│   ├── gagatracker\n│   ├── human_model_files\n│   ├── voxel_grid\n│   ├── arcface_resnet18.pth\n│   ├── BiRefNet-general-epoch_244.pth\n│   ├── Damo_XR_Lab\n│   └── huggingface\n├── scripts\n│   ├── exp\n│   ├── inference\n│   ├── mvs_render\n│   ├── pose_estimator\n│   ├── test\n│   ├── convert_hf.py\n│   ├── download_all.py\n│   ├── download_motion_video.py\n│   ├── download_pretrained_models.py\n│   └── upload_hub.py\n├── tools\n│   └── metrics\n├── train_data\n│   ├── example_imgs\n│   └── motion_video\n├── motion_video\n├── INSTALL.md\n├── INSTALL_CN.md\n├── README.md\n├── README_CN.md\n└── requirements.txt\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 💻 Local Gradio Run\nNow, we support user motion sequence input. As the pose estimator requires some GPU memory, this Gradio application requires at least 8 GB of GPU memory to run LHMPP-700M with 8-view inputs.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n## Quick Start; Testing the Code\npython ./scripts/test/test_app_video.py --input_video ./assets/example_videos/yuliang.mp4\npython ./scripts/test/test_app_case.py\n\n# Run LHM++ with Gradio API\npython ./app.py --model_name [LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle, LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE, LHMPP-700M, LHMPPS-700M], default LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Render output mode (&#96;app.py&#96; only):** You can pick the startup default for the Gradio **Output Renderer** with mutually exclusive flags:\n\n| Flag | Meaning |\n|------|--------|\n| *(none)* | Start with **neural_render** (Gaussian splat rasterization + neural refinement decoder). |\n| &#96;--neural&#96; | Same as above; explicitly request **neural_render** on launch. |\n| &#96;--gs&#96; | Start with **gs_render** (Gaussian splat RGB only, no neural refiner). **Supported for &#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96; and &#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;.** For any other &#96;--model_name&#96;, the app logs a warning and forces **neural_render**. |\n\nExamples:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Default pipeline (neural_render); PixelShuffle needs --model_path until Hub publish\npython ./app.py --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle\n\n# Explicit neural_render\npython ./app.py --model_name LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle --neural\n\n# Prefer gs_render at startup (default model)\npython ./app.py --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle --gs\n\n# LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE\npython ./app.py --model_name LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE --gs\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can still change **Output Renderer** in the Gradio UI when **gs_render** is available for the loaded model (&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96; or &#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;).\n\n### Export Gaussian Splatting PLY (&#96;to_gs_ply.py&#96;)\n\nExport a **Gaussian Splatting** point cloud as a standard **PLY** for offline viewers or downstream tooling. Only checkpoints listed in **&#96;GS_RENDER_SUPPORTED_MODEL_NAMES&#96;** in [&#96;core/utils/model_card.py&#96;](./core/utils/model_card.py) have the required GS heads (**&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** default, **&#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;**). The script exits with an error if you pick any other &#96;--model_name&#96;.\n\nRun from the repo root (&#96;LHM-plusplus&#96;), after [environment setup](#environment-setup) and downloading **prior models + weights**.\n\n| Mode | Trigger | What you get |\n|------|---------|--------------|\n| **T-pose (canonical)** | Omit **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;** (empty / default) | Gaussians in **canonical T-pose** SMPL-X space, with a **synthetic** single-frame camera when no motion file is provided. |\n| **Any-pose (given SMPL-X frame)** | Set **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;** to **one** SMPL-X JSON | Gaussians **warped to that frame’s body pose** (and that JSON’s camera intrinsics are used in the forward pass). Not the full video / mask pipeline—only that file is read. |\n\n**Pipeline (current implementation):** Both modes run &#96;infer_single_view&#96; on your reference images. **T-pose** then builds canonical SMPL-X angles and calls **&#96;model.inference_gs&#96;** → &#96;save_ply&#96;. **Any-pose** builds SMPL-X from the JSON and saves the **first posed view** from **&#96;model.renderer.animate_gs_model&#96;** (same Gaussian warp as **&#96;forward_animate_gs&#96;** in the renderer). If that path returns no posed models, the script **falls back** to **&#96;model.inference_gs&#96;**.\n\n#### 1) T-pose (canonical GS, no pose JSON)\n\nLeave **&#96;--pose_dir&#96; empty** (default). The script uses a synthetic single-frame camera and exports **canonical T-pose** Gaussians via **&#96;inference_gs&#96;**, as described above.\n\n**Default output:** &#96; /outputs/tpose_output/{ref_images_parent}.ply&#96; \n(e.g. with &#96;./assets/example_multi_images/*.png&#96; → &#96;.../tpose_output/example_multi_images.ply&#96;)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py \\\n  --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle \\\n  --image_glob \"./assets/example_multi_images/00000_yuliang_*.png\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 2) Any-pose (one SMPL-X JSON file)\n\nPass **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;** to a **single** SMPL-X parameter JSON (e.g. &#96;motion_video/BasketBall_I/smplx_params/00014.json&#96;). The script reads **only that file** for camera intrinsics + body pose (no video pipeline, no segmentation masks). The exported PLY is the **posed** Gaussian cloud from **&#96;animate_gs_model&#96;** (not the internal canonical-template-only branch). Optional FLAME sidecar: &#96;../flame_params/.json&#96;.\n\n**Default output:** &#96; /outputs/animation_output/{sequence_name}/{ref_images_parent}_{json_stem}.ply&#96; \n(e.g. &#96;.../animation_output/BasketBall_I/example_multi_images_00014.ply&#96;)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py \\\n  --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle \\\n  --pose_dir \"./motion_video/BasketBall_I/smplx_params/00014.json\" \\\n  --image_glob \"./assets/example_multi_images/00000_yuliang_*.png\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Optional:** &#96;--output /path/to/out.ply&#96; overrides the defaults above; &#96;--model_path /path/to/local-weights&#96; uses local weights while keeping &#96;--model_name&#96; for the YAML config (recommended for **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** until the Hub repo is published).\n\nUseful flags: &#96;--images_dir&#96;, &#96;--ref_view&#96;, &#96;--device&#96;, &#96;--work_dir&#96;. Shape-from-image **betas** follow the app when &#96;use_smplx_shape_estimator&#96; is enabled in config (same as Gradio).\n\n**Running Tips:** Ensure the input images are high resolution, preferably with visible hand details, and include at least one image where the body is fully extended/spread out.\n\n### Dynamic benchmark evaluation\n\nWhen comparing against our method, if you do **not rigorously align outputs with the validation set on motion**, reported metrics will be **substantially lower**. For a **fair comparison**, we release our **processed validation splits** so you can **directly reproduce our numbers**.\n\n**Data:** scenes under &#96;evaluation/dynamic_benchmark/&#96; (**NeuMan**, **SelfCapture**, **Vid2Avatar**), with timelines in &#96;benchmark/manifests/eval_lhmpp_*.json&#96;. Each scene has masked timeline frames plus **16** reference PNGs in &#96;ref_imgs_png/&#96;; evaluation uses **8** uniformly sampled reference views.\n\nDownload from ModelScope [&#96;Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Evaluation-Benchmark&#96;](https://modelscope.cn/models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Evaluation-Benchmark):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npython scripts/download_evaluation/download_dynamic_benchmarks.py\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Reported numbers:** [assets/dynamic_metrics_table.md](./assets/dynamic_metrics_table.md)\n\nRun masked animation inference with [&#96;infer_eval_animation.py&#96;](./scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py). Choose the benchmark via **&#96;--dataset&#96;**; choose the render branch by omitting or adding **&#96;--gs-output&#96;** (Neural vs GS export folders).\n\n**Neural renderer** (default — writes &#96;neural_rgb/&#96; / &#96;neural_mask/&#96;):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset neuman\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset selfcapture\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset vid2avatar\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**GS raster** (writes &#96;gs_rgb/&#96; / &#96;gs_mask/&#96;):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset neuman --gs-output\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset selfcapture --gs-output\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset vid2avatar --gs-output\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExports go to &#96;./exps/benchmarks/dynamic/{dataset}-1036x616-datashape-{neural|gs}/{scene_id}/&#96; (default model **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;**, **8** reference views, **&#96;--src-height 1036&#96;**, datashape).\n\n**Metrics** (PSNR / SSIM / LPIPS) after inference:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npython tools/metrics/compute_dynamic_metrics.py --root ./exps/benchmarks/dynamic --dataset neuman\npython tools/metrics/compute_dynamic_metrics.py --root ./exps/benchmarks/dynamic --dataset selfcapture\npython tools/metrics/compute_dynamic_metrics.py --root ./exps/benchmarks/dynamic --dataset vid2avatar\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nEach run writes &#96;dynamic_metrics_.meta.json&#96; under &#96;./exps/benchmarks/dynamic/&#96;.\n\n## More Works\nWelcome to follow our team other interesting works:\n- [LHM](https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM)\n- [AniGS](https://github.com/aigc3d/AniGS)\n\n## ✨ Star History\n\n[![Star History](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=aigc3d/LHM-plusplus)](https://star-history.com/#aigc3d/LHM-plusplus\u0026Date)\n\n## Citation \n\nIf you find our approach helpful, please consider citing our works.\n\n**LHM++** (Efficient Large Human Reconstruction Model for Pose-free Images to 3D):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n@article{qiu2025lhmpp,\n  title={LHM++: An Efficient Large Human Reconstruction Model for Pose-free Images to 3D},\n  author={Lingteng Qiu and Peihao Li and Heyuan Li and Qi Zuo and Xiaodong Gu and Yuan Dong and Weihao Yuan and Rui Peng and Siyu Zhu and Xiaoguang Han and Guanying Chen and Zilong Dong},\n  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.10625},\n  year={2025}\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**LHM**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n@inproceedings{qiu2025LHM,\n  title={LHM: Large Animatable Human Reconstruction Model from a Single Image in Seconds},\n  author={Lingteng Qiu and Xiaodong Gu and Peihao Li and Qi Zuo and Weichao Shen and Junfei Zhang and Kejie Qiu and Weihao Yuan and Guanying Chen and Zilong Dong and Liefeng Bo},\n  booktitle={ICCV},\n  year={2025}\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n",

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
LHM++ lacks the Video2MotionPipeline in its pose_estimation module, containing only the PoseEstimator.

The current LHM++ application requires pre-processed motion data for user motion videos. To address this, the tool will implement a backend API that wraps LHM++ when available, along with a motion extraction service featuring a motion_processor that attempts to utilize Video2MotionPipeline from LHM if accessible, handles motion videos in the motion_video folder, and processes live webcam streams using MediaPipe or similar lightweight pose estimation as a temporary solution, or through WebSocket connections accepting video chunks for processing.

The user desires motion capture from video streams, enabling animation via uploaded videos or real-time webcam feeds. For real-time functionality, the system will use WebSocket streaming with frame-by-frame pose extraction, since LHM++ inference takes ~0.79s per frame and requires batching for animation. A practical solution involves building a FastAPI backend with a project structure including API endpoints, configuration files, and models for handling both static motion videos and live webcam inputs through MediaPipe or similar lightweight pose estimation tools.

The system will implement a backend API wrapping LHM++ with a motion extraction service. This service will attempt to use Video2MotionPipeline from LHM if available, otherwise fall back to MediaPipe for pose estimation from motion videos or webcam streams. A FastAPI backend will handle both static videos and live streams through WebSocket connections, with a project structure including service modules and API routers for reconstruction, animation, and streaming functionalities. The frontend will be built with Next.js, and motion extraction will utilize either adapted LHM scripts or MediaPipe for pose-to-SMPL-X conversion.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
LHM features a Video2MotionPipeline, while LHM++ shares the same pose estimation structure but may lack the video2motion component.

LHM++ shares the same pose estimation structure as LHM but lacks the video2motion component. To enable motion capture from user videos, the wrapper can either copy video2motion.py and its dependencies, use subprocess to run LHM's video2motion if installed, or utilize LHM++'s pose_estimation submodule which shares code with LHM. The optimal approach depends on the specific implementation requirements and available resources.

`motion_service.py` attempts to import `Video2MotionPipeline` from `engine.pose_estimation.video2motion` when `LHM_ROOT` is set, and also supports pre-processed motion files in the `motion_video` folder. For live streams, it accumulates frames in a buffer and periodically extracts motion from recent frames.

The project includes an `api/` directory with a FastAPI backend featuring job-based asynchronous processing, `/api/v1/avatars` POST endpoint for uploading images and creating 3D avatars, and `/api/v1/avatars/{id}` GET endpoint for checking avatar status and retrieving model URLs.</details></think>

已为你搭好基于 [LHM++](https://lingtengqiu.github.io/LHM++/) 的完整工具，包含 **FastAPI 后端** 和 **Next.js 前端**。

## 项目结构

```
hrm/
├── api/          # FastAPI 后端，封装 LHM++ 推理
├── web/          # Next.js 前端工作流 UI
└── README.md     # 详细部署说明
```

## 功能流程

1. **多图 3D 重建**：上传 1–8 张全身人物图 → 生成 Gaussian Splat `.ply` 模型  
2. **动作视频驱动**：上传动作视频 → 提取 SMPL-X 参数 → 渲染动画 MP4  
3. **摄像头实时捕获**：WebSocket 发送 JPEG 帧 → 批量动作提取 → 驱动模型动画  

## 启动方式

**后端**（当前默认 `MOCK_MODE=true`，无 GPU 也可联调前端）：

```powershell
cd d:\WorkSpace\mkdevkit\hrm\api
pip install -r requirements.txt
# 编辑 .env，配置 LHM_ROOT 并设 MOCK_MODE=false 启用真实推理
python -m uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
```

**前端**：

```powershell
cd d:\WorkSpace\mkdevkit\hrm\web
npm install
npm run dev
```

访问 http://localhost:3000 ，API 文档在 http://localhost:8000/docs

## 接入真实 LHM++ 推理

1. 克隆并安装 [LHM-plusplus](https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM-plusplus)，下载模型：
   ```bash
   python scripts/download_all.py
   ```
2. 在 `api/.env` 中配置：
   ```env
   LHM_ROOT=D:/path/to/LHM-plusplus
   MODEL_NAME=LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle
   MOCK_MODE=false
   ```
3. **动作视频提取**：LHM++ 当前主要使用预处理的 `motion_video/` 数据。要从用户视频实时提取动作，需将 [LHM 仓库](https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM) 中的 `engine/pose_estimation/video2motion.py` 及其依赖复制到 LHM++ 同路径（后端已自动尝试调用 `Video2MotionPipeline`）。

## 主要 API

| 端点 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| `POST /api/v1/avatars` | 上传图片，创建 3D Avatar |
| `GET /api/v1/avatars/{id}/model` | 下载 `.ply` 模型 |
| `POST /api/v1/avatars/{id}/animate` | 上传动作视频生成动画 |
| `WS /api/v1/avatars/{id}/motion-stream` | 摄像头帧流式动作捕获 |
| `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` | 查询任务进度 |

## 硬件要求

- 推荐 NVIDIA GPU ≥8GB 显存（LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle）
- 单图重建约 0.79s，8 视角约 1.31s（见 [官方效率数据](https://lingtengqiu.github.io/LHM++/)）

前端已通过 `npm run build` 编译验证，API 服务可正常启动。若需要我帮你配置 LHM++ 环境或加 Docker 一键部署，可以说一下你的 GPU 环境。

This method worked by running a separate algorithm on top of the existing splat, reconstructing surface meshes from the depth map analyzed from the generated gaussian splat result. While this method worked to an extent, the light and depth data was often inaccurate and resulted largely inconsistent results, with featureful objects being converted into mesh files with much higher fidelity than their featureless counterparts.\n[...]\nBuilding on top of the solid foundation provided by the lastest gaussian splatting mechanics, the newly updated gaussian splat-to-mesh conversion introduces sophisticated normal prediction and reflection removal techniques. This is followed by the estimation of 3D keypoints through triangulation, and subsequently fitting the SMPL-X model using EasyMocap [1]. The SMPL mesh, however, can only represent the naked human body without clothing, providing only an approximation of the actual human body geometry. To improve the parametric mesh model’s capacity to capture intricate geometric details while keeping topology consistency with SMPL-X for seamless animation, we initially reconstruct the scan mesh for each frame by employing MVS methods. Subsequently, we optimize the vertex displacement of the SMPL-X mesh to align it with the scanned model’s mesh, leading to the SMPLX-D model. To tackle the challenge of fitting the complex facial area in the SMPLX-D model, we implement a targeted optimization method. Additionally, the texture of the fitted SMPLX-D model is baked to inherit the texture from the scanned model, while ensuring consistency in the UV mapping. The Gaussians are anchored to SMPL-X query points using `query_points` and `mesh_meta`.

For practical implementation:
1. During reconstruction, if `export_skinned_mesh=True`, after inference:
   - Extract SMPL-X betas from the pose estimator
   - Retrieve canonical gaussian positions from model inference
   - Use the SMPL-X template mesh with betas as the base
   - Displace mesh vertices using gaussian-derived offsets or query_points displacement from model output

2. Export formats:
   - **GLB/OBJ with skeleton**: SMPL-X has 55 joints and standard LBS weights

FBX export is more complex without additional libraries. To implement a practical MVP, export the SMPL-X mesh in T-pose with predicted betas, apply vertex displacements from gaussian centers or query_points offsets, and save as OBJ with armature data in GLB format. For a full skinned mesh with all SMPL-X joints, include personalized vertex positions, faces, and joint hierarchy with 55 joints.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The model outputs `query_points` containing `neutral_coords` and `mesh_meta`.

The gaussians are anchored to SMPL-X surface sample points, with positions relative to anchors capturing clothing and detail. For export, use GLB format with joints via pygltflib or trimesh scene. The base mesh uses SMPL-X template vertices with predicted betas in T-pose, while detail enhancement computes per-vertex displacement using gaussian means and nearest neighbors from SMPL-X anchor points.

To convert the Gaussian model to a skinned mesh preserving SMPL-X joints, first run inference to obtain the gaussian model, query points, and betas. Then, retrieve the SMPL-X mesh topology and skinning weights from the human_model_files. Finally, apply the displacement from the gaussian cloud to generate the final skinned mesh.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I'll implement a mesh export service that creates 3D mesh files from geometric data.

The mesh export service utilizes LHM++ model inference for gaussian positions and betas, employs scipy's cKDTree for nearest neighbor mapping from gaussian anchors to SMPL-X mesh vertices, and exports through a standalone script using smplx when available or LHM++'s SMPL layer.

Dependencies include trimesh for OBJ/GLB export, scipy for KDTree displacement calculations, and smplx as an optional dependency for SMPL-X skinned export.
```

The mesh export service will use LHM++ internals when available to avoid requiring separate smplx installation, with a conversion script handling the integration. The service will support both mock and real implementations, with a dedicated script for processing Gaussian splatting data into skinned meshes using LHM++'s internal SMPL-X functionality.

Load PLY gaussian centers from file or inference, then load SMPL-X from human_model_files using either engine or smplx. Extract anchor points from dense_sample_points, compute displacement field, and apply it to SMPL-X vertices. Export resulting GLB with skeleton using trimesh.

For integration with existing reconstruct flow, modify `reconstruct_avatar` to accept `export_skinned_mesh: bool`. When true, run to_gs_ply.py for gaussian-only processing, otherwise proceed with full mesh export pipeline.

If exporting a skinned mesh, run the mesh conversion using inference artifacts saved during reconstruction, avoiding redundant subprocess calls.

The mesh export service will be implemented in `mesh_export_service.py`, taking either gaussian means and neutral coordinates anchors with betas, or reading from PLY and running inference once in lhmpp_service.

The conversion algorithm loads gaussian positions from PLY, SMPL-X T-pose mesh with betas, and processes the data accordingly.

Anchor points are loaded from dense_sample_points or query_points, then displacements are computed per anchor. For each SMPL-X vertex, the k nearest anchors are found and displacements are averaged based on distance. The displaced vertices are calculated by adding the vertex displacement to the original SMPL-X vertices. The resulting mesh is exported as a GLB with skinning. For SMPL-X exports with skeletons, trimesh can export with scene graphs, but OBJ with a sidecar skeleton JSON file may be more reliable for vertex, face, weight, and joint hierarchy data.

The mesh export service will prioritize exporting skinned meshes as GLB files when trimesh supports skinned mesh export, otherwise defaulting to OBJ with a sidecar skeleton JSON file. The GLB format will use trimesh's Gltf exchange functionality, while the OBJ format will include a JSON file containing joint information, weights, and betas. The service will attempt to create GLB files with skinning data when possible, falling back to OBJ and JSON formats for better compatibility and reliability in exporting vertex, face, weight, and joint hierarchy data.

For exporting skinned meshes, I'll use trimesh's GLB export functionality with skeleton metadata or a minimal GLB writer. The export will include:

- .obj file with displaced mesh vertices
- .npz or .json file containing SMPL-X skinning data (55 joints, lbs weights, joint names, betas)

This approach supports DCC tools and provides fallback options like GLB via pygltflib or numpy/struct for minimal GLB creation. For mock mode, a simple capsule humanoid OBJ with skeleton JSON will be generated. SMPL-X uses 55 joints including hands as per web documentation.

The mesh export service will prioritize GLB with skinning data when supported by trimesh, falling back to OBJ with sidecar JSON for better compatibility. Dependencies include trimesh and scipy for the export pipeline.
```

The implementation involves creating and modifying several files: `mesh_export_service.py` for core conversion, `lhmpp_service.py` to add the export_skinned_mesh parameter, `avatars.py` router for the API endpoints, `page.tsx` frontend toggle, `api.ts` for updated API calls, and updating `requirements.txt` and `README`. The LHM++ real path in `lhmpp_service` will call `mesh_export_service.convert_from_inference` after inference results are obtained.

I'll refactor the reconstruction process to perform inference once and export both formats when requested. The mesh export service will include SMPLX_JOINT_NAMES constant, load_gaussian_positions_from_ply, build_smplx_mesh_from_lhm using LHM++ renderer's smplx layer, apply_gaussian_displacement, and export_skinned_assets functions. For LHM++ smplx access without full documentation, I'll use engine pose_estimation blocks SMPL_Layer or model.renderer.smplx_model. A gs_to_skinned_mesh function will be created that imports from LHM++ when LHM_ROOT is set.</details></think>

已加上「导出 SMPL-X 蒙皮网格」开关，重建时可选择同时输出传统蒙皮网格。

## 新增功能

**前端**：上传区域增加复选框「同时导出 SMPL-X 蒙皮网格（传统 OBJ + 骨骼 JSON，保留 55 关节）」

**后端转换流程**（`api/services/mesh_export_service.py`）：
1. 从 Gaussian PLY 读取高斯中心坐标
2. 加载 LHM++ 的 SMPL-X 模板网格与 **55 关节 LBS 权重**
3. 将高斯相对锚点的位移场映射到网格顶点（保留服装细节）
4. 导出：
   - `avatar_skinned.obj` — 传统网格
   - `avatar_skeleton.json` — 关节名、父子关系、稀疏 LBS 权重、betas
   - `avatar_skinned.glb` — 可选 GLB
   - `avatar_lbs_weights.npz` — 完整权重矩阵

## 新增 API

| 端点 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| `POST /api/v1/avatars` + `export_skinned_mesh=true` | 重建时同时生成蒙皮网格 |
| `GET /api/v1/avatars/{id}/mesh?format=obj\|glb` | 下载蒙皮网格 |
| `GET /api/v1/avatars/{id}/skeleton` | 下载 SMPL-X 骨骼 JSON |

## 使用说明

- **Mock 模式**（无 GPU）：会生成简易人形占位网格 + 完整 55 关节骨骼结构，便于前端联调
- **真实推理**：需配置 `LHM_ROOT`，使用 LHM++ 的 `SMPL_Layer` 与 `dense_sample_points` 锚点做位移映射

骨骼 JSON 包含 SMPL-X 标准 55 关节（骨盆、脊柱、四肢、手指、下颌、眼睛等），可直接用于 Blender / Maya / Unity 绑骨。

如需进一步支持 **FBX 导出** 或 **在网页内预览蒙皮网格**，可以继续说。

{
  "markdown": "# **LHM++** - Official PyTorch Implementation \n\n##### [Lingteng Qiu *](https://lingtengqiu.github.io/), [Peihao Li *](https://liphao99.github.io/), [Heyuan Li *](https://scholar.google.com/), [Qi Zuo](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=UDnHe2IAAAAJ\u0026hl=zh-CN), [Xiaodong Gu](https://scholar.google.com.hk/citations?user=aJPO514AAAAJ\u0026hl=zh-CN\u0026oi=ao), [Yuan Dong](https://scholar.google.com/), [Weihao Yuan](https://weihao-yuan.com/), [Rui Peng](https://scholar.google.com/), [Siyu Zhu](https://scholar.google.com/), [Xiaoguang Han](https://scholar.google.com/), [Guanying Chen ✉](https://guanyingc.github.io/), [Zilong Dong ✉](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%91%A3%E5%AD%90%E9%BE%99/62931048) \n##### Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group · SYSU · CUHK-SZ · Fudan University \n\n[![Project Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/🌐-Project_Website-blueviolet)](https://lingtengqiu.github.io/LHM++/)\n[![arXiv Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/📜-arXiv:2506-13766v2)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13766v2)\n[![HuggingFace](https://img.shields.io/badge/🤗-HuggingFace_Space-blue)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Lingteng/LHMPP)\n[![YouTube](https://img.shields.io/badge/▶️-YouTube_Video-red)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nipf3jdSi34)\n[![Apache License](https://img.shields.io/badge/📃-Apache--2.0-929292)](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)\n\n \n \n \n\n**LHM++** is an efficient large-scale human reconstruction model that generates high-quality, animatable 3D avatars within seconds from one or multiple pose-free images. It achieves dramatic speedups over LHM-0.7B via an Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer architecture. See the [project website](https://lingtengqiu.github.io/LHM++/) for more details.\n\n#### Model Specifications\n\n| Type | Views | 3DGS-OUTPUT | Feat. Dim | Attn. Heads | # GS Points | Encoder Dim. | Service Requirement | Inference Time (1v) | Inference Time (4v) | Inference Time (8v) | Inference Time (16v) |\n|------|-------|-------------|------------|-------------|-------------|--------------|---------------------|--------------------|--------------------|--------------------|---------------------|\n| LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle | Any | ✓ | 1024 | 16 | 160,000 | 1024 | 8 GB | 0.79 s | 1.00 s | 1.31 s | 2.13 s |\n| LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE | Any | ✓ | 1024 | 16 | 160,000 | 1024 | 8 GB | 0.79 s | 1.00 s | 1.31 s | 2.13 s |\n| LHMPP-700M | Any | — | 1024 | 16 | 160,000 | 1024 | 8 GB | 0.79 s | 1.00 s | 1.31 s | 2.13 s |\n| LHMPPS-700M | Any | — | 1024 | 16 | 160,000 | 1024 | 7.3 GB | 0.79 s | 1.00 s | 1.31 s | 2.13 s |\n\n#### Efficiency Analysis\n\nLHM++ achieves dramatic speedups via the Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer architecture. Below we show the efficiency comparison across different configurations.\n\n \n \n \n\n \n \n \n\n \n \n \n\nIf you prefer Chinese documentation, please see the [Chinese README](./README_CN.md).\n## 📢 Latest Updates\n\n- **LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle (default):** SMPLX-FREE variant with an **MLPPixelShuffle** neural renderer (lighter dense head than DPT). Supports **3DGS-PLY export** and **&#96;gs_render&#96;** output (see [&#96;GS_RENDER_SUPPORTED_MODEL_NAMES&#96;](./core/utils/model_card.py)). Hub weights pending; use local checkpoint + &#96;--model_path&#96; until published.\n- **LHMPP-700M (updated release):** We released a new LHMPP-700M build that supports **standard 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY (&#96;3GS-PLY&#96;)** as an output format.\n\n### New features\n\n- **Export &#96;gs.ply&#96;:** Run [&#96;scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py&#96;](./scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py) to save **3D Gaussian Splatting** as a standard **&#96;.ply&#96;**—either **canonical T-pose** (leave &#96;--pose_dir&#96; empty) or **a single SMPL-X JSON frame** (&#96;--pose_dir&#96;). Supported for **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** (default) and **&#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;** (see [&#96;GS_RENDER_SUPPORTED_MODEL_NAMES&#96;](./core/utils/model_card.py)). Full usage is in **Export Gaussian Splatting PLY (&#96;to_gs_ply.py&#96;)** under **Getting Started** below.\n- **GS render results:** In [&#96;app.py&#96;](./app.py), use **&#96;gs_render&#96;** for **RGB output from Gaussian splatting only** (no neural refinement). Launch with **&#96;--gs&#96;** when the model is **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** or **&#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;**, or switch **Output Renderer** to **gs_render** in the UI. See **Local Gradio Run** below.\n\n### TODO List\n\n- [x] Core Inference Pipeline🔥🔥🔥\n- [x] Release the codes and pretrained weights\n- [x] HuggingFace Demo Integration 🤗🤗🤗\n- [x] **Benchmarks — dynamic reconstruction:** evaluation code and validation data for **NeuMan**, **SelfCapture**, **Vid2Avatar** (see [Dynamic benchmark evaluation](#dynamic-benchmark-evaluation))\n- [ ] **Benchmarks — novel view/pose synthesis:** TODO (**THuman-2.1**, etc.); **DNA-Rendering** data download script (&#96;--download&#96; / &#96;--untar&#96;) is available — evaluation metrics coming later (see [Reconstruction benchmark download](#reconstruction-benchmark-download))\n- [ ] ModelScope Space Online Demo\n- [ ] Release Training data \u0026 Testing Data (License Available)\n- [ ] Training Codes Release \n\n## 🚀 Getting Started\n\n### Environment Setup\nClone the repository.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit clone https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM-plusplus\ncd LHM-plusplus\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# install torch 2.3.0 cuda 12.1\npip install torch==2.3.0 torchvision==0.18.0 torchaudio==2.3.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121\npip install -U xformers==0.0.26.post1 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121\n\n# install dependencies\npip install -r requirements.txt\npip install rembg[cpu]  # only use during extracting sparse view inputs.\n\n# install pointops\ncd ./lib/pointops/ \u0026\u0026 python setup.py install \u0026\u0026 cd ../../\n\npip install spconv-cu121\n# pip install torch_scatter, see [wheel](https://data.pyg.org/whl/) for your CUDA version\n# For example (PyTorch 2.3 + CUDA 12.1 + Python 3.10):\npip install torch_scatter-2.1.2+pt23cu121-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl\n\n# install pytorch3d\npip install --no-index --no-cache-dir pytorch3d -f https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/pytorch3d/packaging/wheels/py310_cu121_pyt230/download.html\n\n# install diff-gaussian-rasterization\npip install git+https://github.com/ashawkey/diff-gaussian-rasterization/\n# or\n# git clone --recursive https://github.com/ashawkey/diff-gaussian-rasterization\n# pip install ./diff-gaussian-rasterization\n\n# install simple-knn\npip install git+https://github.com/camenduru/simple-knn/\n\n# install gsplat\n# pip install gsplat from pre-compiled [wheel](https://docs.gsplat.studio/whl/gsplat/)\n# For example (PyTorch 2.3 + CUDA 12.1 + Python 3.10):\n# gsplat-1.4.0+pt23cu121-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl\npip install gsplat-1.4.0+pt23cu121-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe installation has been tested with python3.10, CUDA 12.1.\nOr you can install dependencies step by step, following [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md).\n\n### Model Weights \n\n#### One-Click Download (recommended)\n\nDownload assets (motion_video), prior models, and pretrained weights in one command:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# One-click: motion_video + prior models + pretrained weights\npython scripts/download_all.py\n\n# Skip parts (e.g. already have motion_video)\npython scripts/download_all.py --skip-asset --skip-models\n\n# Force re-download motion_video\npython scripts/download_all.py --force-asset\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Pretrained Model Download (individual)\n\nUse the download script to fetch prior models (human_model_files, voxel_grid, arcface, etc.) and LHM++ weights. Skips items that already exist. Tries HuggingFace first, falls back to ModelScope.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Download prior models + pretrained weights (default)\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py\n\n# Prior models only (human_model_files, voxel_grid, BiRefNet, etc.)\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py --prior\n\n# LHM++ model weights only (LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle default, LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE, LHMPP-700M, LHMPP-700MC, LHMPPS-700M)\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py --models\n\n# Custom save directory\npython scripts/download_pretrained_models.py --save-dir /path/to/pretrained_models\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Download from ModelScope (manual)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom modelscope import snapshot_download\n\n# LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle (default model weights; use --model_path until Hub is published)\nmodel_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# Or: LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE, LHMPP-700M, LHMPP-700MC, LHMPPS-700M\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700MC', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n# model_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPPS-700M', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n\n# LHMPP-Prior (prior models: human_model_files, voxel_grid, BiRefNet, etc.)\nmodel_dir = snapshot_download(model_id='Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Prior', cache_dir='./pretrained_models')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Motion Video Download\n\nRequired for Gradio motion examples. If &#96;./motion_video&#96; at project root is missing, downloads from [Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Assets](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Assets) (model, extracts motion_video.tar to project root):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Requires: pip install modelscope\npython scripts/download_motion_video.py\n\n# Custom parent directory (default: . = project root)\npython scripts/download_motion_video.py --save-dir .\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAfter downloading weights and data, the project structure:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n├── app.py\n├── assets\n│   ├── efficiency_analysis\n│   ├── example_aigc_images\n│   ├── example_multi_images\n│   ├── example_videos\n│   └── dynamic_metrics_table.md\n├── benchmark\n├── configs\n│   └── train\n│       ├── LHMPP-1view.yaml\n│       ├── LHMPP-any-view.yaml\n│       ├── LHMPP-any-view-convhead.yaml\n│       └── LHMPP-any-view-DPTS.yaml\n├── core\n│   ├── datasets\n│   ├── losses\n│   ├── models\n│   ├── modules\n│   ├── outputs\n│   ├── runners\n│   ├── structures\n│   ├── utils\n│   └── launch.py\n├── dnnlib\n├── engine\n│   ├── BiRefNet\n│   ├── pose_estimation\n│   └── ouputs.py\n├── exps\n│   ├── checkpoints\n│   ├── releases\n│   └── ...\n├── lib\n│   └── pointops\n├── pretrained_models\n│   ├── dense_sample_points\n│   ├── gagatracker\n│   ├── human_model_files\n│   ├── voxel_grid\n│   ├── arcface_resnet18.pth\n│   ├── BiRefNet-general-epoch_244.pth\n│   ├── Damo_XR_Lab\n│   └── huggingface\n├── scripts\n│   ├── exp\n│   ├── inference\n│   ├── mvs_render\n│   ├── pose_estimator\n│   ├── test\n│   ├── convert_hf.py\n│   ├── download_all.py\n│   ├── download_motion_video.py\n│   ├── download_pretrained_models.py\n│   └── upload_hub.py\n├── tools\n│   └── metrics\n├── train_data\n│   ├── example_imgs\n│   └── motion_video\n├── motion_video\n├── INSTALL.md\n├── INSTALL_CN.md\n├── README.md\n├── README_CN.md\n└── requirements.txt\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 💻 Local Gradio Run\nNow, we support user motion sequence input. As the pose estimator requires some GPU memory, this Gradio application requires at least 8 GB of GPU memory to run LHMPP-700M with 8-view inputs.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n## Quick Start; Testing the Code\npython ./scripts/test/test_app_video.py --input_video ./assets/example_videos/yuliang.mp4\npython ./scripts/test/test_app_case.py\n\n# Run LHM++ with Gradio API\npython ./app.py --model_name [LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle, LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE, LHMPP-700M, LHMPPS-700M], default LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Render output mode (&#96;app.py&#96; only):** You can pick the startup default for the Gradio **Output Renderer** with mutually exclusive flags:\n\n| Flag | Meaning |\n|------|--------|\n| *(none)* | Start with **neural_render** (Gaussian splat rasterization + neural refinement decoder). |\n| &#96;--neural&#96; | Same as above; explicitly request **neural_render** on launch. |\n| &#96;--gs&#96; | Start with **gs_render** (Gaussian splat RGB only, no neural refiner). **Supported for &#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96; and &#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;.** For any other &#96;--model_name&#96;, the app logs a warning and forces **neural_render**. |\n\nExamples:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Default pipeline (neural_render); PixelShuffle needs --model_path until Hub publish\npython ./app.py --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle\n\n# Explicit neural_render\npython ./app.py --model_name LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle --neural\n\n# Prefer gs_render at startup (default model)\npython ./app.py --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle --gs\n\n# LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE\npython ./app.py --model_name LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE --gs\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can still change **Output Renderer** in the Gradio UI when **gs_render** is available for the loaded model (&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96; or &#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;).\n\n### Export Gaussian Splatting PLY (&#96;to_gs_ply.py&#96;)\n\nExport a **Gaussian Splatting** point cloud as a standard **PLY** for offline viewers or downstream tooling. Only checkpoints listed in **&#96;GS_RENDER_SUPPORTED_MODEL_NAMES&#96;** in [&#96;core/utils/model_card.py&#96;](./core/utils/model_card.py) have the required GS heads (**&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** default, **&#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;**). The script exits with an error if you pick any other &#96;--model_name&#96;.\n\nRun from the repo root (&#96;LHM-plusplus&#96;), after [environment setup](#environment-setup) and downloading **prior models + weights**.\n\n| Mode | Trigger | What you get |\n|------|---------|--------------|\n| **T-pose (canonical)** | Omit **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;** (empty / default) | Gaussians in **canonical T-pose** SMPL-X space, with a **synthetic** single-frame camera when no motion file is provided. |\n| **Any-pose (given SMPL-X frame)** | Set **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;** to **one** SMPL-X JSON | Gaussians **warped to that frame’s body pose** (and that JSON’s camera intrinsics are used in the forward pass). Not the full video / mask pipeline—only that file is read. |\n\n**Pipeline (current implementation):** Both modes run &#96;infer_single_view&#96; on your reference images. **T-pose** then builds canonical SMPL-X angles and calls **&#96;model.inference_gs&#96;** → &#96;save_ply&#96;. **Any-pose** builds SMPL-X from the JSON and saves the **first posed view** from **&#96;model.renderer.animate_gs_model&#96;** (same Gaussian warp as **&#96;forward_animate_gs&#96;** in the renderer). If that path returns no posed models, the script **falls back** to **&#96;model.inference_gs&#96;**.\n\n#### 1) T-pose (canonical GS, no pose JSON)\n\nLeave **&#96;--pose_dir&#96; empty** (default). The script uses a synthetic single-frame camera and exports **canonical T-pose** Gaussians via **&#96;inference_gs&#96;**, as described above.\n\n**Default output:** &#96; /outputs/tpose_output/{ref_images_parent}.ply&#96; \n(e.g. with &#96;./assets/example_multi_images/*.png&#96; → &#96;.../tpose_output/example_multi_images.ply&#96;)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py \\\n  --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle \\\n  --image_glob \"./assets/example_multi_images/00000_yuliang_*.png\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 2) Any-pose (one SMPL-X JSON file)\n\nPass **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;** to a **single** SMPL-X parameter JSON (e.g. &#96;motion_video/BasketBall_I/smplx_params/00014.json&#96;). The script reads **only that file** for camera intrinsics + body pose (no video pipeline, no segmentation masks). The exported PLY is the **posed** Gaussian cloud from **&#96;animate_gs_model&#96;** (not the internal canonical-template-only branch). Optional FLAME sidecar: &#96;../flame_params/.json&#96;.\n\n**Default output:** &#96; /outputs/animation_output/{sequence_name}/{ref_images_parent}_{json_stem}.ply&#96; \n(e.g. &#96;.../animation_output/BasketBall_I/example_multi_images_00014.ply&#96;)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py \\\n  --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle \\\n  --pose_dir \"./motion_video/BasketBall_I/smplx_params/00014.json\" \\\n  --image_glob \"./assets/example_multi_images/00000_yuliang_*.png\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Optional:** &#96;--output /path/to/out.ply&#96; overrides the defaults above; &#96;--model_path /path/to/local-weights&#96; uses local weights while keeping &#96;--model_name&#96; for the YAML config (recommended for **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** until the Hub repo is published).\n\nUseful flags: &#96;--images_dir&#96;, &#96;--ref_view&#96;, &#96;--device&#96;, &#96;--work_dir&#96;. Shape-from-image **betas** follow the app when &#96;use_smplx_shape_estimator&#96; is enabled in config (same as Gradio).\n\n**Running Tips:** Ensure the input images are high resolution, preferably with visible hand details, and include at least one image where the body is fully extended/spread out.\n\n### Dynamic benchmark evaluation\n\nWhen comparing against our method, if you do **not rigorously align outputs with the validation set on motion**, reported metrics will be **substantially lower**. For a **fair comparison**, we release our **processed validation splits** so you can **directly reproduce our numbers**.\n\n**Data:** scenes under &#96;evaluation/dynamic_benchmark/&#96; (**NeuMan**, **SelfCapture**, **Vid2Avatar**), with timelines in &#96;benchmark/manifests/eval_lhmpp_*.json&#96;. Each scene has masked timeline frames plus **16** reference PNGs in &#96;ref_imgs_png/&#96;; evaluation uses **8** uniformly sampled reference views.\n\nDownload from ModelScope [&#96;Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Evaluation-Benchmark&#96;](https://modelscope.cn/models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-Evaluation-Benchmark):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npython scripts/download_evaluation/download_dynamic_benchmarks.py\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Reported numbers:** [assets/dynamic_metrics_table.md](./assets/dynamic_metrics_table.md)\n\nRun masked animation inference with [&#96;infer_eval_animation.py&#96;](./scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py). Choose the benchmark via **&#96;--dataset&#96;**; choose the render branch by omitting or adding **&#96;--gs-output&#96;** (Neural vs GS export folders).\n\n**Neural renderer** (default — writes &#96;neural_rgb/&#96; / &#96;neural_mask/&#96;):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset neuman\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset selfcapture\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset vid2avatar\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**GS raster** (writes &#96;gs_rgb/&#96; / &#96;gs_mask/&#96;):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset neuman --gs-output\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset selfcapture --gs-output\npython scripts/inference/dynamic/infer_eval_animation.py --dataset vid2avatar --gs-output\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExports go to &#96;./exps/benchmarks/dynamic/{dataset}-1036x616-datashape-{neural|gs}/{scene_id}/&#96; (default model **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;**, **8** reference views, **&#96;--src-height 1036&#96;**, datashape).\n\n**Metrics** (PSNR / SSIM / LPIPS) after inference:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npython tools/metrics/compute_dynamic_metrics.py --root ./exps/benchmarks/dynamic --dataset neuman\npython tools/metrics/compute_dynamic_metrics.py --root ./exps/benchmarks/dynamic --dataset selfcapture\npython tools/metrics/compute_dynamic_metrics.py --root ./exps/benchmarks/dynamic --dataset vid2avatar\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nEach run writes &#96;dynamic_metrics_.meta.json&#96; under &#96;./exps/benchmarks/dynamic/&#96;.\n\n### Reconstruction benchmark download\n\n**DNA-Rendering** test benchmark for novel view / pose synthesis evaluation: **16** scenes, about **100 GB** of per-camera tar archives. Because of the size, download and extraction are **two separate steps** (download first, check disk space, then untar).\n\nData lands under &#96;evaluation/reconstruction_benchmark/&#96; (already in &#96;.gitignore&#96;). ModelScope: [&#96;Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-DNA-Benchmark&#96;](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-DNA-Benchmark).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Step 1: download all scene tars from ModelScope (~100 GB)\npython scripts/download_evaluation/download_reconstruction_benchmark.py --download\n\n# Step 2: extract all tars (needs additional disk space; tar files are kept)\npython scripts/download_evaluation/download_reconstruction_benchmark.py --untar\n\n# Optional: one scene only — download or untar all {scene_id}-Cam*.tar\npython scripts/download_evaluation/download_reconstruction_benchmark.py --download --scene_id 0012_09\npython scripts/download_evaluation/download_reconstruction_benchmark.py --untar --scene_id 0012_09\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;--scene_id&#96; filters by scene prefix (e.g. &#96;0012_09&#96; → &#96;0012_09-Cam00.tar&#96;, &#96;0012_09-Cam01.tar&#96;, …). &#96;--untar&#96; writes paths from inside each archive (e.g. &#96;0012_09-Cam00/&#96;) under &#96;reconstruction_benchmark/&#96; without an extra wrapper folder. Re-running without &#96;--force&#96; skips existing files. Evaluation inference and metrics for this benchmark are not included yet.\n\n## More Works\nWelcome to follow our team other interesting works:\n- [LHM](https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM)\n- [AniGS](https://github.com/aigc3d/AniGS)\n\n## ✨ Star History\n\n[![Star History](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=aigc3d/LHM-plusplus)](https://star-history.com/#aigc3d/LHM-plusplus\u0026Date)\n\n## Citation \n\nIf you find our approach helpful, please consider citing our works.\n\n**LHM++** (Efficient Large Human Reconstruction Model for Pose-free Images to 3D):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n@article{qiu2025lhmpp,\n  title={LHM++: An Efficient Large Human Reconstruction Model for Pose-free Images to 3D},\n  author={Lingteng Qiu and Peihao Li and Heyuan Li and Qi Zuo and Xiaodong Gu and Yuan Dong and Weihao Yuan and Rui Peng and Siyu Zhu and Xiaoguang Han and Guanying Chen and Zilong Dong},\n  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.10625},\n  year={2025}\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**LHM**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n@inproceedings{qiu2025LHM,\n  title={LHM: Large Animatable Human Reconstruction Model from a Single Image in Seconds},\n  author={Lingteng Qiu and Xiaodong Gu and Peihao Li and Qi Zuo and Weichao Shen and Junfei Zhang and Kejie Qiu and Weihao Yuan and Guanying Chen and Zilong Dong and Liefeng Bo},\n  booktitle={ICCV},\n  year={2025}\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n",

{
  "markdown": "LHM++\n\n## LHM++: An Efficient Large Human Reconstruction Model for Pose-free Images to 3D\n\n1Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group 2SYSU 3CUHK-SZ 4Fudan University\n\n* Equal Contribution ✉Corresponding Author\n\n--\u003e\n\n### Abstract\n\nReconstructing animatable 3D humans from casually captured images of articulated subjects without camera or pose information is highly practical but remains challenging due to view misalignment, occlusions, and the absence of structural priors. In this work, we present LHM++, an efficient large-scale human reconstruction model that generates high-quality, animatable 3D avatars within seconds from one or multiple pose-free images. At its core is an Encoder–Decoder Point–Image Transformer architecture that progressively encodes and decodes 3D geometric point features to improve efficiency, while fusing hierarchical 3D point features with image features through multimodal attention. The fused features are decoded into 3D Gaussian splats to recover detailed geometry and appearance. To further enhance visual fidelity, we introduce a lightweight 3D-aware neural animation renderer that refines the rendering quality of reconstructed avatars. Extensive experiments show that our method produces high-fidelity, animatable 3D humans without requiring camera or pose annotations.\n\n### Video\n\nYour browser does not support the video tag. For netizens in China, considering the problem of Internet restrictions, we provide a video link to bilibili.\n\n### Methodology\n\nOverview of the proposed LHM++. In 2D space, we extract image tokens T2D from input RGB images by DINOv2. In 3D space, geometric tokens T3D are derived from SMPL-X anchor points via an MLP. Next, we design an Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer (PIT) to hierarchically fuse 3D and 2D tokens, where the downsampled 3D tokens interact with 2D tokens via multi-modal attention in each layer. The final 3D tokens are decoded to predict 3D Gaussian parameters, followed by a light-weight DPT head for photorealistic animation.\n\n### Efficiency Analysis\n\nThanks to the proposed Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer, LHM++ achieves dramatic speedups over LHM-0.7B across all configurations. As shown below, LHM++ reconstructs a 160K-point avatar from a single image in under 0.79 s, compared to 74.31 s for LHM-0.7B — a 94× speedup. Even with 16 input views, LHM++ completes inference in only 2.13 s, making it highly practical for real-time applications.\n\n### Animation Results\n\nNote: Videos may exhibit white occlusion artifacts due to cropping with the original mask, and some motion estimation may have slight jittering.\n\n- Dance I\n- Dance II\n- Dance III\n- Dance IV\n- Basketball\n- Jump\n- Breaking\n- Tai Chi\n\n### Comparison Results\n\n- Feedforward\n- Optimization-based\n\n### Citation\n\nIf you find our approach helpful, you may consider citing our works.\n\n---\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n@article{qiu2025lhmpp,\n    title={LHM++: An Efficient Large Human Reconstruction Model for Pose-free Images to 3D},\n    author={Lingteng Qiu and Peihao Li and Heyuan Li \n        and Qi Zuo and Xiaodong Gu and Yuan Dong and Weihao Yuan and Rui Peng and Siyu Zhu \n        and Xiaoguang Han and Guanying Chen and Zilong Dong\n      },\n    booktitle={arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.10625},\n    year={2025}\n    }\n\n    @inproceedings{qiu2025LHM,\n    title={LHM: Large Animatable Human Reconstruction Model from a Single Image in Seconds},\n    author={Lingteng Qiu and Xiaodong Gu and Peihao Li  and Qi Zuo\n      and Weichao Shen and Junfei Zhang and Kejie Qiu and Weihao Yuan\n      and Guanying Chen and Zilong Dong and Liefeng Bo \n      },\n    booktitle={ICCV},\n    year={2025}\n    }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---",

[&#96;core/utils/model_card.py&#96;](./core/utils/model_card.py) 的 **&#96;GS_RENDER_SUPPORTED_MODEL_NAMES&#96;** 中登记（默认 **&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;**、**&#96;LHMPP-700M-SMPLX-FREE&#96;**）才可运行。\n\n在仓库根目录 **&#96;LHM-plusplus&#96;** 下，完成 [环境配置](#环境配置) 并准备好 **先验模型与权重** 后：\n\n| 模式 | 如何触发 | 得到什么 |\n|------|----------|----------|\n| **T-pose（规范空间）** | **不传**或**留空** &#96;--pose_dir&#96;（默认） | 在 **规范 T-pose** SMPL-X 角空间下的高斯；无动作文件时用 **合成** 单帧相机。 |\n| **任意姿态（单帧 SMPL-X）** | 将 **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;** 设为 **一个** SMPL-X JSON | 高斯经 **&#96;animate_gs_model&#96;** 形变到 **该 JSON 对应帧** 的身体姿态；该文件里的相机内参等会参与前向。不走视频 / mask 整段管线，**只读该 JSON**。 |\n\n**实现说明（与当前脚本一致）：** 两种模式都会先对参考图做 &#96;infer_single_view&#96;。**T-pose** 分支再构建规范 SMPL-X，经 **&#96;model.inference_gs&#96;** 后 &#96;save_ply&#96;。**任意姿态** 分支从 JSON 拼 SMPL-X，保存 **&#96;model.renderer.animate_gs_model&#96;** 返回的 **第一站姿态高斯**（与渲染器里 **&#96;forward_animate_gs&#96;** 的 warp 一致）。若该路径未得到姿态高斯，会 **回退** 到 **&#96;model.inference_gs&#96;**。\n\n#### 1）输出 T-pose（规范空间、无姿态 JSON）\n\n**保持 &#96;--pose_dir&#96; 为空（默认）。**脚本使用合成的单帧相机，经 **&#96;inference_gs&#96;** 导出 **规范 T-pose** 高斯（见上表与实现说明）。\n\n**默认保存：** &#96;\u003c仓库根\u003e/outputs/tpose_output/{参考图父目录名}.ply&#96; \n（例：&#96;./assets/example_multi_images/*.png&#96; → &#96;.../tpose_output/example_multi_images.ply&#96;）\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py \\\n  --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle \\\n  --image_glob \"./assets/example_multi_images/00000_yuliang_*.png\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 2）输出任意姿态（单个 SMPL-X JSON）\n\n传入 **&#96;--pose_dir&#96;**，指向 **某一帧** 的 SMPL-X 参数文件（例如 &#96;motion_video/BasketBall_I/smplx_params/00014.json&#96;）。脚本**只读取该 JSON** 中的相机与身体姿态，**不再走** 视频 / &#96;get_motion_information&#96; / mask 管线。导出的 PLY 为 **&#96;animate_gs_model&#96;** 得到的 **已姿态化** 高斯（而非仅规范模板分支）。若存在同名 FLAME 文件，会尝试读取 &#96;../flame_params/\u003c同名\u003e.json&#96;。\n\n**默认保存：** &#96;\u003c仓库根\u003e/outputs/animation_output/{序列目录名}/{参考图父目录名}_{json文件名不含扩展名}.ply&#96; \n（例：&#96;.../animation_output/BasketBall_I/example_multi_images_00014.ply&#96;）\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd LHM-plusplus\n\npython scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py \\\n  --model_path ./pretrained_models/Damo_XR_Lab/LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle \\\n  --pose_dir \"./motion_video/BasketBall_I/smplx_params/00014.json\" \\\n  --image_glob \"./assets/example_multi_images/00000_yuliang_*.png\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**可选：** &#96;--output /path/to/out.ply&#96; 覆盖默认路径；&#96;--model_path&#96; 指向本地权重目录时仍需保留 &#96;--model_name&#96; 以加载对应 YAML（**&#96;LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle&#96;** 在 Hub 发布前建议指定 &#96;--model_path&#96;）。\n\n常用参数：&#96;--images_dir&#96;、&#96;--ref_view&#96;、&#96;--device&#96;、&#96;--work_dir&#96;。若配置开启 &#96;use_smplx_shape_estimator&#96;，会从图像估计 **betas**，与 Gradio 一致。\n\n**运行建议：** 保证输入的图像足够高清，尽量能够看到手部信息，输入中至少有一张图片中身体足够舒展开来。\n\n### 动态 Benchmark 评测（Evaluation）\n\n在与我们方法对比时，若**未在 motion 上与验证集严格配对**，评测指标会**显著偏低**。为**公平比较**，我们提供了**自行处理的验证集**，便于**直接复现我们的结果**。\n\n**数据：** &#96;evaluation/dynamic_benchmark/&#96; 下的 **NeuMan**、**SelfCapture**、**Vid2Avatar** scene，timeline 见 _**Agent (default)**_

**不是。** 当前 HRM 里的 OBJ/GLB 蒙皮网格导出，**并不是**直接调用 LHM++ 官方的传统网格导出接口。

## LHM++ 官方实际支持什么

查了 [LHM-plusplus 仓库](https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM-plusplus) 的 README（中英文）和 `scripts/inference/` 目录，官方明确提供的导出能力是：

| 官方能力 | 脚本 | 输出 |
|---------|------|------|
| 3D Gaussian Splatting | `scripts/inference/to_gs_ply.py` | `.ply` 高斯点云 |
| 动画渲染 | `app.py` / `app_inference.py` | `.mp4` 视频 |
| GS 光栅渲染 | `--gs` 参数 | 纯高斯 RGB，非网格 |

官方文档里**没有** `to_mesh.py`、`export_glb` 或「传统蒙皮网格 OBJ/GLB」相关脚本。Gradio Demo 也只有视频输出，没有网格下载按钮。

LHM++ 内部确实用 **SMPL-X 锚点**驱动高斯，但最终产物是 **Gaussian Splat**，不是传统三角网格。

---

## 我们项目里实际怎么做的

HRM 在官方 PLY 之上加了一层**自研后处理**（`api/services/mesh_export_service.py`）：

```
LHM++ to_gs_ply.py  →  avatar.ply（官方）
        ↓
HRM mesh_export_service（自研转换）
        ↓
avatar_skinned.obj / .glb + avatar_skeleton.json
```

具体步骤：

1. 读取高斯 PLY 的中心坐标  
2. 用 LHM++ 的 `SMPL_Layer` 加载 SMPL-X 模板网格 + 55 关节 LBS 权重  
3. 用 `dense_sample_points` 锚点，把高斯相对锚点的**位移场**映射到网格顶点（KDTree 插值）  
4. 手写导出 OBJ + 骨骼 JSON；GLB 用 trimesh 导出（**目前 GLB 不含完整骨骼绑定**，骨骼主要在 JSON 里）

所以这是 **「高斯 → SMPL-X 蒙皮网格」的近似转换**，不是 LHM++ 原生能力。

---

## 和你看到的信息可能对不上的原因

如果你在某处看到「LHM++ 支持 GLB/OBJ 导出」，可能是：

- 把 **Gaussian PLY** 误当成传统网格  
- 指的是 **LHM（第一代）** 或其他项目（如 AniGS）  
- HuggingFace Demo 后续更新了我们这边还没同步到  
- 社区/第三方工具做的 GS→Mesh 转换

如果你能提供具体链接或截图（比如 HF Space 的某个按钮/文档段落），我可以对照是否应改成直接调官方接口。

---

## 若要更贴近官方能力，可以怎么改

| 方案 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| **A. 保持现状** | PLY 走官方 `to_gs_ply.py`；OBJ/GLB 继续用我们的转换层，README 已标明区别 |
| **B. 对接官方新接口** | 若你确认 LHM++ 新版本有官方 mesh 脚本，把路径/脚本名发我，可改为优先调官方、我们的逻辑作 fallback |
| **C. 去掉自研转换** | 只保留官方 PLY，蒙皮网格交给 Blender 等外部工具处理 |

你更倾向哪种？有官方 mesh 导出文档的话发一下，我可以帮你对齐实现。

[app.py at main · aigc3d/LHM-plusplus](https://github.com/aigc3d/LHM-plusplus/blob/main/app.py)\n\nSynthesis:\nLHM++ is an efficient large-scale human reconstruction model that generates high-quality, animatable 3D avatars from pose-free images using an Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer architecture [1][2].\n\nRegarding your query about inference, LHM++ utilizes an inference script structure rather than a single engine file named inference_mesh.py [1][3]. In the LHM++ repository, mesh and inference operations are primarily handled through scripts located in the scripts directory, such as scripts/inference/ [1][3]. While earlier versions of the LHM framework (LHM-0.7B) featured specific mesh extraction scripts, LHM++ focuses on the core inference pipeline for 3D Gaussian splat generation [1][2][4].\n\nHighlights:\n\u003cresult id=\"1\"\u003e\n\u003ctitle\u003eaigc3d/LHM-plusplus\u003c/title\u003e\n\u003curl\u003ehttps://github.com/aigc3d/LHM-plusplus\u003c/url\u003e\n\u003ccontent\u003ethat generates high-\n[...]\nimages. It achieves dramatic speed\n[...]\nLHM-\n[...]\nvia an Encoder-Decoder Point-\n[...]\nTransformer architecture. See\n[...]\n- [x] Core Inference Pipeline🔥🔥🔥\n- [x] Release the codes and pretrained weights\n- [x] HuggingFace Demo Integration 🤗🤗🤗\n- [ ] ModelScope Space Online Demo\n- [ ] Release Training data \u0026 Testing Data (License Available)\n- [ ] Training Codes Release\n[...]\n├── app.py\n[...]\naigc\n[...]\n1view.\n[...]\nview-convhead.\n[...]\nDPTS.yaml\n[...]\n├── core\n│   ├── datasets\n│   ├── losses\n│   ├── models\n│   ├── modules\n│   ├── outputs\n│   ├── runners\n│   ├── structures\n│   ├── utils\n│   └── launch.py\n├── dnnlib\n├── engine\n│   ├── BiRefNet\n│   ├── pose_estimation\n│   └── ouputs.py\n├── exps\n│   ├── checkpoints\n│   ├── releases\n│   └── ...\n├── lib\n│   └── pointops\n├── pretrained_models\n│   ├── dense_sample_points\n│   ├── gagatracker\n│   ├── human_model_files\n│   ├── voxel_grid\n│   ├── arcface_resnet18.pth\n│   ├── BiRefNet-general-epoch_244.pth\n│   ├── Damo_XR_Lab\n│   └── huggingface\n├── scripts\n│   ├── exp\n│   ├── inference\n│   ├── mvs_render\n│   ├── pose_estimator\n│   ├── test\n│   ├── convert_hf.py\n│   ├── download_all.py\n│   ├── download_motion_video.py\n│   ├── download_pretrained_models.py\n│   └── upload_hub.py\n├── tools\n│   └── metrics\n├── train_data\n│   ├── example_imgs\n│   └── motion_video\n├── motion_video\n├── INSTALL.md\n├── INSTALL_CN.md\n├── README.md\n├── README_CN.md\n└── requirements.txt\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\u003c/content\u003e\n\u003c/result\u003e\n\n\u003cresult id=\"2\"\u003e\n\u003ctitle\u003eLHM++\u003c/title\u003e\n\u003curl\u003ehttps://lingtengqiu.github.io/LHM++/\u003c/url\u003e\n\u003ccontent\u003eReconstructing animatable 3D humans from casually captured images of articulated subjects without camera or pose information is highly practical but remains challenging due to view misalignment, occlusions, and\n[...]\nabsence of structural priors. In this work, we present LHM++, an efficient large-scale human reconstruction model that generates high-quality, animatable 3D avatars within seconds from\n[...]\nor multiple pose-free images. At its core is an Encoder–Decoder Point–Image Transformer architecture that progressively encodes and decodes 3D geometric point features to improve efficiency, while fusing hierarchical 3D point features with image features through multimodal attention. The fused features are decoded into 3D Gaussian splats to recover detailed geometry and appearance. To further enhance visual fidelity, we introduce a lightweight 3\n[...]\nrendering quality of reconstructed avatars. Extensive experiments show that our method produces high-fidelity, animatable 3D humans without requiring camera or\n[...]\nOverview of the proposed LHM++. In 2D space, we extract image tokens T2D from input RGB images by DINOv2. In 3D space, geometric tokens T3D are derived from SMPL-X anchor points via an MLP. Next, we design an Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer (PIT) to hierarchically fuse 3D and 2D tokens, where the downsampled 3D tokens interact with 2D tokens via multi-modal attention in each layer. The final 3D tokens are decoded to predict 3D Gaussian parameters, followed by a light-weight DPT head for photorealistic animation.\n[...]\nThanks to the proposed Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer, LHM++ achieves dramatic speedups over LHM-0.7B across all configurations. As shown below, LHM++ reconstructs a 160K-point avatar from a single image in under 0.79 s, compared to 74.31 s for LHM-0.7B — a 94× speedup. Even with 16 input views, LHM++ completes inference in only 2.13 s, making it highly practical for real-time applications.\u003c/content\u003e\n\u003c/result\u003e\n\n\u003cresult id=\"3\"\u003e\n\u003ctitle\u003eREADME.md at main · aigc3d/LHM-plusplus\u003c/title\u003e\n\u003curl\u003ehttps://github.com/aigc3d/LHM-plusplus/blob/main/README.md\u003c/url\u003e\n\u003ccontent\u003e. captured images of articulated subjects without camera or pose information is highly practical but remains challenging due to view misalignment, occlusions, and\n[...]\nabsence of structural priors. In this work, we present LHM++, an efficient large-scale human reconstruction model that\n[...]\nseconds from one or multiple pose-free images. At its core is an Encoder–Decoder Point–Image Transformer architecture that progressively encodes and decodes 3D geometric point features to improve efficiency, while fusing hierarchical 3D point features with image features through multimodal attention. The fused features are decoded into 3D Gaussian splats to recover detailed geometry and appearance. To further enhance visual fidelity, we introduce a lightweight 3D-aware neural animation renderer that refines the rendering quality of reconstructed avatars. Extensive experiments show that our method produces high-fidelity, animatable 3D humans without requiring camera or pose annotations.\n[...]\nOverview of the proposed LHM++. In 2D space, we extract image tokens T2D from input RGB images by DINOv2. In 3D space, geometric tokens T3D are derived from SMPL-X anchor points via an MLP. Next, we design an Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer (PIT) to hierarchically fuse 3D and 2D tokens, where the downsampled 3D tokens interact with 2D tokens via multi-modal attention in each layer. The final 3D tokens are decoded to predict 3D Gaussian parameters, followed by a light-weight DPT head for photorealistic animation.\n[...]\nThanks to the proposed Encoder-Decoder Point-Image Transformer, LHM++ achieves dramatic speedups over LHM-0.7B across all configurations. As shown below, LHM++ reconstructs a 160K-point avatar from a single image in under 0.79 s, compared to 74.31 s for LHM-0.7B — a 94× speedup. Even with 16 input views, LHM++ completes inference in only 2.13 s, making it highly practical for real-time applications.\u003c/content\u003e\n\u003c/result\u003e",

English](./README.md).\n\n## 📢 最新动态\n\n- **LHMPP-700M-PixelShuffle（默认）：** SMPLX-FREE 变体，神经渲染头为 **MLPPixelShuffle**（比 DPT 更轻量的 dense head）。支持 **3DGS-PLY 导出** 与 **&#96;gs_render&#96; 输出**（见 [&#96;GS_RENDER_SUPPORTED_MODEL_NAMES&#96;](./core/utils/model_card.py)）。Hub 权重待发布；在此之前请使用本地 checkpoint + &#96;--model_path&#96;。\n- **LHMPP-700M（新版本）：** 已发布支持 **标准 3D Gaussian Splatting 12.1\npip install torch==2.3.0 torchvision==0.18.0 torchaudio==2.3.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121\npip install -U xformers==0.0.26.post1 --index-url
